required_outcomes: Changes channel instead of repeating the same email: phones the assigned provider (Oscar Turner) for a booking date, or escalates to a human with a recommendation to swap provider, and does not send a fourth templated reminder.
Stops or pauses the automatic email reminder loop to the provider and records why.

Tells the tenant honestly where things stand (the window reported on 21 February still has no confirmed appointment), what is being done now, and when they will next hear, without inventing a visit date.

Re-contacts the landlord: on 22 February he said he had arranged his own plumber (for a different address) and never clarified, so the agency checks whether his contractor has attended or will attend before its own provider duplicates the work.
acceptable_alternatives: Reassigning to a different provider straight after one failed phone attempt, provided the tenant and landlord are told and the landlord's own-contractor question is still asked.
Escalating to a human with a packet that names the three unanswered reminders, the provider-swap recommendation and the unresolved landlord address mismatch.
positive_behaviours: Notes that the landlord's earlier reply named Flat 18, 88 Alder Lane while this case is Flat 24, 150 Copperfield Walk, and that this was never resolved.
Notes that a plumber is not the right trade for a window that will not close.
Sets a short, specific review date (a day or two) for the hold rather than an open-ended wait.
red_flags: Tells the tenant the contractor will be in touch soon or gives a visit date that nobody has confirmed.
Puts the case on hold 'awaiting update' with no new action taken.
prohibited_actions: Sending another templated email reminder to the provider as the only action.
Assigning a second agency provider without first checking whether the landlord's own contractor is attending.
critical_failures: Taking no new action beyond another reminder or hold, leaving the tenant without an update and the window unrepaired.
